notes.text: Morgan Frost is day to day (upper-body injury) and missed their last game.

Kevin Bahl is out for the season and has missed the last 10 games. Joel Hanley has taken his spot beside Šimon Nemec. That pair has had 42% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 128:31 together, about what it had with Bahl (46%).
Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 24 games, up from 2% last season.
Anthony Mantha is on long-term injured reserve (neck injury) and has missed the last 8 games.
Johnathan Kovacevic is on injured reserve (ankle injury) and has missed the last 6 games.

stakes: The Flames go in tied for fourth in the Pacific with 24 points, the Devils second in the Metropolitan with 34 points.

NJD.head: A big edge for the Devils
NJD.body: New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Flames’ best way in is keeping dangerous shots away.

CGY.head: The Flames have their work cut out
CGY.body: New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. To pull this off, the Flames can start with keeping dangerous shots away, plus Dustin Wolf stealing the show.

story.head: Nemec returns to New Jersey
paras: The Devils have won two in a row, and the Flames (11-13-2) beat Pittsburgh 6-3 on Wednesday. Going in, the Flames are fourth in the Pacific (tied for 21st in the NHL) and the Devils second in the Metropolitan (sixth).

The Flames play some of the league’s fastest games (2nd), take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd) and take more penalties than they draw (30th). The Devils, by contrast, draw more penalties than they take (3rd). Calgary has scored 2.58 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. As for the Devils, they rarely throw hits (2nd lowest) and keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest). Something has to give when the Flames’ shooting runs into the Devils’ defense, and the Flames’ struggling power play gets a tough test from the Devils’ penalty killers.

Joel Farabee (8 G / 13 A / 21 P in 26 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, and Matt Coronato (6 G / 12 A / 18 P in 26 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Devils, Jack Hughes (10 G / 20 A / 30 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Jesper Bratt (4 G / 19 A / 23 P in 25 GP) isn’t far behind.
Dustin Wolf (6-6-2 / .878 SV% in 14 GS) is expected to start for Calgary, and Jake Allen (6-5-0 / .873 SV% in 10 GS) for New Jersey.
The Devils usually control more of the chances than the Flames do.
